100.$description: Extends the numeric scale to cover a value the Bloom design actually uses. Added rather than rounding the design onto a scale that was never designed for it.

1-5.$description: Half step. The hyphen stands for the decimal point, so radius/1-5 is 1.5px. It exists because the design really uses it, not because the scale wanted it.

2-5.$description: Rounded from a fractional value left by a rescale() on the diagram zoom control. The change is under half a pixel; the point is that the value is now a token.

row-padding-x.$description: Horizontal padding of a sidebar nav row.

row-gap.$description: Gap between a sidebar row icon and its label.

row-height.$description: Height of a sidebar nav row, collapsed and expanded alike.

border.$description: Documentation callout note border. Light and dark come from the mode, never from a variant.

border.$description: Documentation callout danger border. Light and dark come from the mode, never from a variant.

foreground.$description: Code sample text. The code surface is dark in both themes, so this token does not change with the mode.

background.$description: Code sample surface. Dark in both themes by design, so the pale code text always reads.

scrim.$description: Backdrop behind a modal or overlay.

modal.$description: Scrim behind a modal dialog. The alpha lives IN the token, so a binding pass can never flatten it. 55%: the page stays readable but is clearly out of reach. Same value in all four modes: a scrim is dark in the light theme too.

panel.$description: Scrim behind a side drawer or a slide-over panel. Lighter than a modal: the page behind stays workable context, not a blocked surface. Same value in all four modes: a scrim is dark in the light theme too.

menu.$description: Click-catcher behind a menu, a dropdown or an anchored popover. Fully transparent on purpose: it exists to catch the click that closes the menu, never to tint the screen. Same value in all four modes: a scrim is dark in the light theme too.
